description:
RETIRED on 2026-10-30 (0.96.0): a refusing stub that changes nothing, and every call to it is counted; at the re-count (about 2026-12-23) it is deleted if nobody called it and restored if somebody did. Call `dimension_drifts` with `target_id` and `dimension`, which reads that one node's drift exactly as this did.

Quality-dimension drift for ONE target node: the recorded observations of a single `-ility` (reliability, performance, maintainability …) on that node over time, and whether the latest reading is worse than the one before. A NULL VALUE SAYS WHICH NULL: the reply distinguishes a legal dimension with no observations recorded on this node, a node that does not exist, and a dimension name the schema does not declare — three facts that used to share `{"value": null}`. `dimension_drifts` (plural) sweeps the whole design worst-first. Ask for this when you want to know whether one part of the design is getting worse on one quality axis.

target_id.description:
The assessed node — any node type carrying `HAS_OBSERVATION` edges
to `DimensionObservation` records.

name: dimension_drift
title: Quality Drift of One Node (Retired)
